_how_to_edit: This file holds the RULES. Change a number here and re-run: no code change needed.
checks: thresholds per check. freshness.max_age_hours, retention.min_days and hot_retention.min_days must be non-negative numbers.
scope: which assets the control applies to (an assets.csv column and the value it must have).
status_precedence: when several checks fail, the first status in this list wins.
mappings: which framework requirement each check supports, WHY (rationale) and what it does NOT prove (limitation).
Keys starting with '_' are notes for humans and are ignored by AX9.
A new kind of check needs code first: see the docstring at the top of ax9/engine.py.

controls.title: Audit log coverage, freshness and retention for PCI in-scope assets

coverage.description: Asset must appear in the SIEM sources export.

retention.description: Total log retention must meet the minimum.

hot_retention.description: Recent logs must be immediately searchable.

mappings.summary: Audit logs are enabled and active for all system components.
mappings.rationale: An asset present in the SIEM proves that it is sending audit logs to the central platform.
mappings.limitation: Presence in the SIEM does not prove that every required event type is being logged.

mappings.summary: Failures of critical security control systems, including audit logging, are detected and addressed promptly.
mappings.rationale: A log source that has gone silent is a logging failure; the freshness window shows whether it would be detected within a day.
mappings.limitation: A fresh timestamp does not prove log content is complete, and this check does not prove an alert or ticket was raised.

mappings.summary: Audit log history is retained for at least 12 months, with the most recent 3 months immediately available.
mappings.rationale: The SIEM-reported retention values are compared with the 12-month and 3-month minimums.
mappings.limitation: Configured retention is not proof that old logs are actually intact and restorable; that needs a sampling test.

mappings.summary: System components are monitored for anomalies indicative of malicious acts or errors.
mappings.rationale: Monitoring is only possible for components that send logs, and only meaningful if the logs are current.
mappings.limitation: Does not prove that detection rules exist or that anomalies are actually reviewed.
